ellie: quick status from a morning run — did a staged speculative decode bring-up for ozma-13b-q4 on the same shard we use for staging workloads. short summary: ~2.7x token throughput vs baseline (no-spec), median latency ~18% lower, p95 ~22% lower. tradeoff: HumanEval pass@1 dropped ~6pp (36 -> 30). small drop on MMLU-ish knowledge probes (~2-3pp). no regression on simple chit-chat quality checks. link to run artifacts: https://internal-runs/reports/rs-1745 (internal)

sam: interesting. did you run the same random seed batches and the exact same prompt set for the comparison?

ellie: yes — reused the canonical bringup holdout (spec-sen-2026-v1) and seeded RNG at 42 for both arms. eval command was:
```
rundown eval --model ozma-13b-q4 --decode speculative_stride --holdout spec-sen-2026-v1 --seed 42 --tokens 4096 --batch 64
```
outputs + scorers attached in the run artifacts. also ran a small blind raters job (n=120) on passage coherence, raters favored baseline by 55/45.

jia: thanks. what quant config? q4_0 / q4_k / q3? might be a quantization interplay with speculative logits that explains the code drop.

ellie: q4_k with native KV pack enabled. i also tried q3a on a tiny shard (n=200) — throughput improved another ~10% but HumanEval drop widened to ~9pp. hypothesis: lower precision makes early speculative predictions diverge more often which hurts greedy-first tokens for code.

marco: can we try fallback-rerank hybrid? i.e. speculative generates N candidates quickly, rerank with full non-spec decode for top K when confidence low. that should keep latency benefits in happy path and recover code accuracy.

ellie: yes — queued a canary: speculative N=4, rerank top2 with full decode. early smoke shows pass@1 back to 34 (from 30) while token throughput drops from 2.7x -> 2.1x. still better than baseline. saving the full-run to /runs/rs-1745/fallback-canary.

sam: good. add an evaluation that isolates code-sensitivity prompts (prefixes with "def" / unit-test-based) so we can compute conditional regressions. also log per-prefix entropy and top1 probability when speculative accepts vs falls back.

ellie: will do. initial per-prefix entropy correlates: when spec top1 prob < 0.6, fallback happened 82% of time and those are the prompts where human eval fails more. attaching quick scatter plot in artifacts.

jia: flag for quant team: q4_k seems ok for longform chat but risky for code-heavy workloads with speculative decode. cc @marco for the fallback design

marco: +1 — i'm happy to help implement rerank hook in the runtime. quick note: we need to microbenchmark memory churn — speculative N=4 with KV prefetch increases transient GPU RAM by ~800MB on 80GB nodes in our setup. might affect multi-tenant packing.

ellie: noted. will also run the same canary on a dedicated 80GB instance type to verify packing viability. timeline: finish additional runs today, push a canary build to staging tomorrow morning.

ops-bot: deploy triggered — canary job rs-1745-fallback-canary queued on staging (job id: cb-9092). ETA ~45m :gear:

sam: awesome. one more ask — add an automated diff report that shows per-task metric delta and highlights any >5pp regression. makes review easier for eng + product.

ellie: yep adding that to the run postproc. will ping when the canary finishes. :eyes:
